1. TRUTH is the base that bears the earth; by Surya are the heavens sustained.
By Law the Adityas stand secure, and Soma holds his place in heaven.
2. By Soma are the Adityas strong, by Soma mighty is the earth.
Thus Soma in the midst of all these constellations hath his place.
3. One thinks, when they have brayed the plant, that he hath drunk the Soma's juice;
Of him whom Brahmans truly know as Soma no one ever tastes.
paragraphs.original: सोमं यं ब्रह्माणो विदुर्न तस्याश्नाति कश्चन
paragraphs.translit: somaṃ yaṃ brahmāṇo vidurna tasyāśnāti kaścana

paragraphs.text: 4. Soma, secured by sheltering rules, guarded by hymns in Brhati,
Thou standest listening to the stones none tastes of thee who dwells on earth.
5. When they begin to drink thee then, O God, thou swellest out again.
paragraphs.original: यत्त्वा देव प्रपिबन्ति तत आ प्यायसे पुनः ।
paragraphs.translit: yattvā deva prapibanti tata ā pyāyase punaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Vayu is Soma's guardian God. The Moon is that which shapes the years.
paragraphs.original: वायुः सोमस्य रक्षिता समानां मास आकृतिः
paragraphs.translit: vāyuḥ somasya rakṣitā samānāṃ māsa ākṛtiḥ

paragraphs.text: 6. Raibhi was her dear bridal friend, and Narasamsi led her home.
Lovely was Surya's robe: she came to that which Gatha had adorned.
7. Thought was the pillow of her couch, sight was the unguent for her eyes:
paragraphs.original: चित्तिरा उपबर्हणं चक्षुरा अभ्यञ्जनम् । द्यौर्भूमिः कोश आसीद्यदयात्सूर्या पतिम्
paragraphs.translit: cittirā upabarhaṇaṃ cakṣurā abhyañjanam | dyaurbhūmiḥ kośa āsīdyadayātsūryā patim

paragraphs.text: Her treasury was earth and heaven when Surya went unto her Lord.
The bridesmen were the Asvin Pair Agni was leader of the train.
9. Soma was he who wooed the maid: the groomsmen were both Asvins, when
The Sun-God Savitar bestowed his willing Surya on her Lord.
10. Her spirit was the bridal car; the covering thereof was heaven:
Bright were both Steers that drew it when Surya approached her husband's, home.
11. Thy Steers were steady, kept in place by holy verse and Sama-hymn:
All car were thy two chariot wheels: thy path was tremulous in the sky,
paragraphs.original: श्रोत्रं ते चक्रे आस्तां दिवि पन्थाश्चराचारः
paragraphs.translit: śrotraṃ te cakre āstāṃ divi panthāścarācāraḥ

paragraphs.text: 12. Clean, as thou wentest, were thy wheels wind, was the axle fastened there.
paragraphs.original: शुची ते चक्रे यात्या व्यानो अक्ष आहतः ।
paragraphs.translit: śucī te cakre yātyā vyāno akṣa āhataḥ |

paragraphs.text: Surya, proceeding to her Lord, mounted a spirit-fashioned car.
13. The bridal pomp of Surya, which Savitar started, moved along.
In Magha days are oxen slain, in Arjuris they wed the bride.
14. When on your three-wheeled chariot, O Asvins, ye came as wooers unto Surya's bridal,
Then all the Gods agreed to your proposal Pusan as Son elected you as Fathers.
paragraphs.original: विश्वे देवा अनु तद्वामजानन्पुत्रः पितराववृणीत पूषा
paragraphs.translit: viśve devā anu tadvāmajānanputraḥ pitarāvavṛṇīta pūṣā

paragraphs.text: 15. O ye Two Lords of lustre, then when ye to Surya's wooing came,
Where was one chariot wheel of yours? Where stood ye for die Sire's command?
16. The Brahmans, by their seasons, know, O Surya, those two wheels of thine:
paragraphs.original: द्वे ते चक्रे सूर्ये ब्रह्माण ऋतुथा विदुः ।
paragraphs.translit: dve te cakre sūrye brahmāṇa ṛtuthā viduḥ |

paragraphs.text: One kept concealed, those only who are skilled in highest truths have learned.
17. To Surya and the Deities, to Mitra and to Varuna.
Who know aright the thing that is, this adoration have I paid.
paragraphs.original: ये भूतस्य प्रचेतस इदं तेभ्योऽकरं नमः
paragraphs.translit: ye bhūtasya pracetasa idaṃ tebhyo'karaṃ namaḥ

paragraphs.text: 18. By their own power these Twain in close succession move;
paragraphs.original: पूर्वापरं चरतो माययैतौ शिशू क्रीळन्तौ परि यातो अध्वरम् । विश्वान्यन्यो भुवनाभिचष्ट ऋतूँरन्यो विदधज्जायते पुनः
paragraphs.translit: pūrvāparaṃ carato māyayaitau śiśū krīḷantau pari yāto adhvaram | viśvānyanyo bhuvanābhicaṣṭa ṛtūm̐ranyo vidadhajjāyate punaḥ

paragraphs.text: They go as playing children round the sacrifice.
One of the Pair beholdeth all existing things; the other ordereth seasons and is born again.
19. He, born afresh, is new and new for ever ensign of days he goes before the Mornings
Coming, he orders f6r the Gods their portion. The Moon prolongs the days of our existence.
paragraphs.original: भागं देवेभ्यो वि दधात्यायन्प्र चन्द्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः
paragraphs.translit: bhāgaṃ devebhyo vi dadhātyāyanpra candramāstirate dīrghamāyuḥ

paragraphs.text: 20. Mount this, all-shaped, gold-hued, with strong wheels, fashioned of Kimsuka and Salmali, light-rolling,
paragraphs.original: सुकिंशुकं शल्मलिं विश्वरूपं हिरण्यवर्णं सुवृतं सुचक्रम् ।
paragraphs.translit: sukiṃśukaṃ śalmaliṃ viśvarūpaṃ hiraṇyavarṇaṃ suvṛtaṃ sucakram |

paragraphs.text: Bound for the world of life immortal, Surya: make for thy lord a happy bridal journey.
paragraphs.original: आ रोह सूर्ये अमृतस्य लोकं स्योनं पत्ये वहतुं कृणुष्व
paragraphs.translit: ā roha sūrye amṛtasya lokaṃ syonaṃ patye vahatuṃ kṛṇuṣva

paragraphs.text: 21. Rise up from hence: this maiden hath a husband. I laud Visvavasu with hymns and homage.
paragraphs.original: उदीर्ष्वातः पतिवती ह्येषा विश्वावसुं नमसा गीर्भिरीळे ।
paragraphs.translit: udīrṣvātaḥ pativatī hyeṣā viśvāvasuṃ namasā gīrbhirīḷe |

paragraphs.text: Seek in her father's home another fair one, and find the portion from of old assigned thee.
paragraphs.original: अन्यामिच्छ पितृषदं व्यक्तां स ते भागो जनुषा तस्य विद्धि
paragraphs.translit: anyāmiccha pitṛṣadaṃ vyaktāṃ sa te bhāgo januṣā tasya viddhi

paragraphs.text: 22. Rise up from hence, Visvavasu: with reverence we worship thee.
Seek thou another willing maid, and with her husband leave the bride.
paragraphs.original: अन्यामिच्छ प्रफर्व्यं सं जायां पत्या सृज
paragraphs.translit: anyāmiccha prapharvyaṃ saṃ jāyāṃ patyā sṛja

paragraphs.text: 23. Straight in direction be the paths, and thornless, whereon our fellows travel to the wooing.
paragraphs.original: अनृक्षरा ऋजवः सन्तु पन्था येभिः सखायो यन्ति नो वरेयम् ।
paragraphs.translit: anṛkṣarā ṛjavaḥ santu panthā yebhiḥ sakhāyo yanti no vareyam |

paragraphs.text: Let Aryaman and Bhaga lead us: perfect, O Gods, the union of the wife and husband.
paragraphs.original: समर्यमा सं भगो नो निनीयात्सं जास्पत्यं सुयममस्तु देवाः
paragraphs.translit: samaryamā saṃ bhago no ninīyātsaṃ jāspatyaṃ suyamamastu devāḥ

paragraphs.text: 24. Now from the noose of Varuna I free thee, wherewith Most Blessed Savitar hath bound thee.
paragraphs.original: प्र त्वा मुञ्चामि वरुणस्य पाशाद्येन त्वाबध्नात्सविता सुशेवः ।
paragraphs.translit: pra tvā muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśādyena tvābadhnātsavitā suśevaḥ |

paragraphs.text: In Law's seat, to the world of virtuous action, I give thee up uninjured with thy consort.
paragraphs.original: ऋतस्य योनौ सुकृतस्य लोकेऽरिष्टां त्वा सह पत्या दधामि
paragraphs.translit: ṛtasya yonau sukṛtasya loke'riṣṭāṃ tvā saha patyā dadhāmi

paragraphs.text: 25. Hence, and not thence, I send these free. I make thee softly fettered there.
That, Bounteous Indra, she may live blest in her fortune and her sons.
26. Let Pusan take thy hand and hence conduct thee; may the two Asvins on their car transport thee.
paragraphs.original: पूषा त्वेतो नयतु हस्तगृह्याश्विना त्वा प्र वहतां रथेन ।
paragraphs.translit: pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyāśvinā tvā pra vahatāṃ rathena |

paragraphs.text: Go to the house to be the household's mistress and speak as lady ito thy gathered people.
paragraphs.original: गृहान्गच्छ गृहपत्नी यथासो वशिनी त्वं विदथमा वदासि
paragraphs.translit: gṛhāngaccha gṛhapatnī yathāso vaśinī tvaṃ vidathamā vadāsi

paragraphs.text: 27. Happy be thou and prosper with thy children here: be vigilant to rule thy household in this home.
paragraphs.original: इह प्रियं प्रजया ते समृध्यतामस्मिन्गृहे गार्हपत्याय जागृहि ।
paragraphs.translit: iha priyaṃ prajayā te samṛdhyatāmasmingṛhe gārhapatyāya jāgṛhi |

paragraphs.text: Closely unite thy body with this; man, thy lord. So shall ye, full of years, address your company.
paragraphs.original: एना पत्या तन्वं सं सृजस्वाधा जिव्री विदथमा वदाथः
paragraphs.translit: enā patyā tanvaṃ saṃ sṛjasvādhā jivrī vidathamā vadāthaḥ

paragraphs.text: 28. Her hue is blue and red: the fiend who clingeth close is driven off.
Well thrive the kinsmen of this bride the husband is bound fast in bonds.
29. Give thou the woollen robe away: deal treasure to the Brahman priests.
paragraphs.original: परा देहि शामुल्यं ब्रह्मभ्यो वि भजा वसु ।
paragraphs.translit: parā dehi śāmulyaṃ brahmabhyo vi bhajā vasu |

paragraphs.text: This female fiend hath got her feet, and as a wife attends her lord.
paragraphs.original: कृत्यैषा पद्वती भूत्व्या जाया विशते पतिम्
paragraphs.translit: kṛtyaiṣā padvatī bhūtvyā jāyā viśate patim

paragraphs.text: 30. Unlovely is his body when it glistens with this wicked fiend,
What time the husband wraps about his limbs the garment of his wife.
31. Consumptions, from her people, which follow the bride's resplendent train,-
paragraphs.original: ये वध्वश्चन्द्रं वहतुं यक्ष्मा यन्ति जनादनु ।
paragraphs.translit: ye vadhvaścandraṃ vahatuṃ yakṣmā yanti janādanu |

paragraphs.text: These let the Holy Gods again bear to the place from which they came.
32. Let not the highway thieves who lie in ambush find the wedded pair.
By pleasant ways let them escape the danger, and let foes depart.
33. Signs of good fortune mark the bride come all of you and look at her.
Wish her prosperity, and then return unto your homes again.
34. Pungent is this, and bitter this, filled, as it were, with arrow-barbs, Empoisoned and not fit for use.
The Brahman who knows Surya well deserves the garment of the bride.
35. The fringe, the cloth that decks her head, and then the triply parted robe,-
Behold the hues which Surya wears these doth the Brahman purify.
paragraphs.original: सूर्यायाः पश्य रूपाणि तानि ब्रह्मा तु शुन्धति
paragraphs.translit: sūryāyāḥ paśya rūpāṇi tāni brahmā tu śundhati

paragraphs.text: 36. I take thy hand in mine for happy fortune that thou mayst reach old age with me thy husband.
paragraphs.original: गृभ्णामि ते सौभगत्वाय हस्तं मया पत्या जरदष्टिर्यथासः ।
paragraphs.translit: gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā jaradaṣṭiryathāsaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Gods, Aryaman, Bhaga, Savitar, Purandhi, have given thee to be my household's mistress.
paragraphs.original: भगो अर्यमा सविता पुरंधिर्मह्यं त्वादुर्गार्हपत्याय देवाः
paragraphs.translit: bhago aryamā savitā puraṃdhirmahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya devāḥ

paragraphs.text: 37. O Pusan, send her on as most auspicious, her who shall be the sharer of my pleasures;
paragraphs.original: तां पूषञ्छिवतमामेरयस्व यस्यां बीजं मनुष्या वपन्ति ।
paragraphs.translit: tāṃ pūṣañchivatamāmerayasva yasyāṃ bījaṃ manuṣyā vapanti |

paragraphs.text: Her who shall twine her loving arms about me, and welcome all my love and mine embraces.
paragraphs.original: या न ऊरू उशती विश्रयाते यस्यामुशन्तः प्रहराम शेपम्
paragraphs.translit: yā na ūrū uśatī viśrayāte yasyāmuśantaḥ praharāma śepam

paragraphs.text: 38. For thee, with bridal train, they, first, escorted Surya to her home.
Give to the husband in return, Agni, the wife with progeny.
paragraphs.original: पुनः पतिभ्यो जायां दा अग्ने प्रजया सह
paragraphs.translit: punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṃ dā agne prajayā saha

paragraphs.text: 39. Agni hath given the bride again with splendour and with ample life.
paragraphs.original: पुनः पत्नीमग्निरदादायुषा सह वर्चसा । दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जीवाति शरदः शतम्
paragraphs.translit: punaḥ patnīmagniradādāyuṣā saha varcasā | dīrghāyurasyā yaḥ patirjīvāti śaradaḥ śatam

paragraphs.text: Long lived be he who is her lord; a hundred autumns let him live.
Agni was thy third husband: now one born of woman is thy fourth.
41. Soma to the Gandharva, and to Agni the Gandharva gave:
And Agni hath bestowed on me riches and sons and this my spouse.
42. Be ye not parted; dwell ye here reach the full time of human life.
paragraphs.original: इहैव स्तं मा वि यौष्टं विश्वमायुर्व्यश्नुतम् ।
paragraphs.translit: ihaiva staṃ mā vi yauṣṭaṃ viśvamāyurvyaśnutam |

paragraphs.text: With sons and grandsons sport and play, rejoicing in your own abode.
43. So may Prajapati bring children forth to us; may Aryaman adorn us till old age come nigh.
paragraphs.original: आ नः प्रजां जनयतु प्रजापतिराजरसाय समनक्त्वर्यमा ।
paragraphs.translit: ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu prajāpatirājarasāya samanaktvaryamā |

paragraphs.text: Not inauspicious enter thou thy husband's house: bring blessing to our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
paragraphs.original: अदुर्मङ्गलीः पतिलोकमा विश शं नो भव द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे
paragraphs.translit: adurmaṅgalīḥ patilokamā viśa śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade

paragraphs.text: 44. Not evil-eyed, no slayer of thy husband, bring weal to cattle, radiant, gentlehearted;
Loving the Gods, delightful, bearing heroes, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds.
paragraphs.original: वीरसूर्देवकामा स्योना शं नो भव द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे
paragraphs.translit: vīrasūrdevakāmā syonā śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade

paragraphs.text: 45. O Bounteous Indra, make this bride blest in her sons and fortunate.
paragraphs.original: इमां त्वमिन्द्र मीढ्वः सुपुत्रां सुभगां कृणु ।
paragraphs.translit: imāṃ tvamindra mīḍhvaḥ suputrāṃ subhagāṃ kṛṇu |

paragraphs.text: Vouchsafe to her ten sons, and make her husband the eleventh man.
46. Over thy husband's father and thy husband's mother bear full sway.
paragraphs.original: सम्राज्ञी श्वशुरे भव सम्राज्ञी श्वश्र्वां भव ।
paragraphs.translit: samrājñī śvaśure bhava samrājñī śvaśrvāṃ bhava |

paragraphs.text: Over the sister of thy lord, over his brothers rule supreme.
paragraphs.original: ननान्दरि सम्राज्ञी भव सम्राज्ञी अधि देवृषु
paragraphs.translit: nanāndari samrājñī bhava samrājñī adhi devṛṣu

paragraphs.text: 47. So may the Universal Gods, so may the Waters join our hearts.
paragraphs.original: समञ्जन्तु विश्वे देवाः समापो हृदयानि नौ ।
paragraphs.translit: samañjantu viśve devāḥ samāpo hṛdayāni nau |

paragraphs.text: May Matarisvan, Dhatar, and Destri together bind us close.
paragraphs.original: सं मातरिश्वा सं धाता समु देष्ट्री दधातु नौ
paragraphs.translit: saṃ mātariśvā saṃ dhātā samu deṣṭrī dadhātu nau
